info.title: PPC Research API
info.description:
Access real-time paid search intelligence and SERP analysis to uncover competitor advertising strategies and identify high-value keyword opportunities. Powered by SpyFu's unmatched paid search data collection spanning 18 years of continuous advertising intelligence across global markets.

SpyFu's PPC Research API delivers **20x more paid keywords per domain** than SEMRush or Ahrefs, built on a foundation of **8 billion keywords** with comprehensive advertising metrics and **18 years of historical advertising data**. Our live SERP tracking captures every paid search result with **updates every 15 seconds**, ensuring you have real-time competitive advertising intelligence across all 28 supported countries.

While competitors provide basic paid keyword snapshots, SpyFu offers complete advertising timeline data with live updates every 15 seconds. Our database contains 18 years of paid search history compared to competitors' limited 5-year snapshots with 1/20th the data volume per domain.

With this API, you can analyze live paid search results and competitor ad positioning, identify high-converting keywords through SERP analysis, track competitor ad spend and strategy changes, discover new paid search opportunities before competitors, monitor ad copy variations and testing patterns, and analyze SERP features impact on paid search performance. Access real-time bidding intelligence to understand market competition dynamics and optimize your ad campaigns based on competitor insights.

The PPC Research API integrates seamlessly with SpyFu's Ad History API for complete advertising intelligence, combining live SERP data with historical ad copy analysis and campaign evolution tracking.

Get started with comprehensive API documentation and interactive examples at [SpyFu Developer Portal](https://developer.spyfu.com).

get.description:
Returns paid search results (ads) that a domain appears in across Google search. This endpoint reveals the competitive paid landscape to identify advertising opportunities and understand competitor PPC strategies.

[Visualize this API live on SpyFu](https://www.spyfu.com/ppc/keywords/domain?query=amazon.com)

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: Domain to analyze for paid search presence.

x-enumDescriptions.SearchVolume: Number of searches done this past month on Google.com (or within selected country). Blended from multiple sources for better snapshot of search activity
x-enumDescriptions.KeywordDifficulty: PPC ranking difficulty score (0-100 scale, higher = more difficult to rank). Based on advertiser competition, cost-per-click, and bid density for paid search results
x-enumDescriptions.AdPosition: Average position where the domain's ads appear in paid search results (1 = top ad position)
x-enumDescriptions.AdCount: Total number of advertisers seen over the last 6 months for this keyword
x-enumDescriptions.DateSearched: Most recent date this keyword data was updated in SpyFu's database

parameters.name: startingRow
parameters.description: Row number to start the results with.

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description: The maximum number of rows returned.

parameters.name: countryCode
parameters.description: Country market to search.  Specifically, this maps to the Google domain version to query against (e.g., google.com for US, google.de for Germany, etc.).

parameters.name: adultFilter
parameters.description: Exclude adult keywords considered unsafe for work.

parameters.name: onlyAdultKeywords
parameters.description: Only include adult keywords considered unsafe for work.

parameters.name: excludeHomepageKeywords
parameters.description: Exclude keywords that rank on the homepage of the searched domain.

parameters.name: adCount.min
parameters.description: Filter by the number of total advertisers.

parameters.name: adCount.max
parameters.description: Filter by the number of total advertisers.

parameters.name: searchVolume.min
parameters.description: Filter by the number of searches done this past month on Google.com

parameters.name: searchVolume.max
parameters.description: Filter by the number of searches done this past month on Google.com

parameters.name: includeTerms
parameters.description: CSV of terms that are required to be in the results.

parameters.name: excludeTerms
parameters.description: CSV of terms that are required to not be in the results.

200.description: Successfully retrieved paid search results for the domain. Returns a paginated list of keywords where the domain appears in paid ads with position and competition data.

schema.description: Response wrapper containing paid SERP keyword results with pagination metadata and total result counts.

results.description: Array of paid search keywords with comprehensive SERP data and performance metrics.

keyword.description: The keyword that triggers this paid ad result.

termId.description: Unique identifier for this keyword in SpyFu's database.

adPosition.description: Position where the ad appears on the search results page (1 = top position).

adCount.description: Total number of ads this domain has for this keyword.

dateSearched.description: Date when this keyword was first discovered and added to SpyFu's database.

title.description: Headline text of the paid search result as it appears in SERPs.

bodyHtml.description: HTML content of the ad description and additional text displayed in the search result.

domain.description: Domain name of the advertiser placing this paid search ad.

searchVolume.description: Monthly search volume for this keyword based on Google search data across the selected country/region.

keywordDifficulty.description: SEO difficulty score (1-100) indicating how challenging it would be to rank organically for this keyword, with 100 being most difficult.

isNsfw.description: Indicates whether the search result contains content that may not be safe for work environments.

items.description: Represents a paid search keyword with comprehensive SERP data including search volume, keyword difficulty, and ad positioning metrics.

totalMatchingResults.description: Total number of paid keywords available that match the query criteria, including results not included in the current page.

400.description: Bad Request - Invalid parameters provided (e.g., invalid domain format, pageSize exceeds maximum, or invalid country code)

401.description: Unauthorized - Invalid API credentials or insufficient permissions to access PPC keyword data

500.description: Internal Server Error - A server-side error occurred while processing the request

Basic_Authentication_Token.description:
Basic Authentication is a standard that involves encoding your SPYFU_API_ID:SECRET_KEY into a Base64 string. Your SpyFu API ID and Secret Key can both be found under the Account Settings -> API Usage page. Additionally, you can find the Base64 string has been pre-generated on the same page under Base 64 Key. Finally, this encoded string is sent in the "Authorization" header prefixed with the keyword "Basic":
For example, to authorize as 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000:AB12WXYZ the client would send
Authorization: Basic MDAwMDAwMDAtMDAwMC0wMDAwLTAwMDAtMDAwMDAwMDAwMDAwOkFCMTJXWFla

Query_Parameter_Token.description:
An API key can be added as a query parameter. Your API key is listed as "Secret Key" found under the Account Settings -> API Usage page
For example, to authorize with the API key AB12WXY
/apis/example_api/GetExample?domain=spyfu.com&api_key=AB12WXYZ
Query_Parameter_Token.name: api_key

HMAC_Authentication_Header.description:
For even more security, each request can be individually authenticated with a timestamped HMAC (Hash Message Authentication Code) signature. Composed of your secret key, a valid timestamp, the API request path, and all request parameters.

Creating the signature:


Combine the pieces that will be converted into the signature.
StringToSign =
	HTTP-Verb + "
" +
	Timestamp + "
" +
	UrlPath + "
"
	QueryParameters;

Create UTF-8 encodings of the above string and of your secret key.
byte[] SecretKeyBytes = UTF-8-Encoding-Of( Upper-Case-Of( SECRET_KEY ) );
byte[] StringToSignBytes = UTF-8-Encoding-Of( StringToSign );

Use an implementation of HMAC256 using your UTF-8 secret key to encode the combined string of your request. This should then be converted to Base64 to finish creating your signature.
Signature = Base64( HMAC-SHA256( SecretKeyBytes, StringToSignBytes ) );

Using the signature:


This signature is then sent in through an Authentication header with your username.
Authentication: UserName:Signature
HMAC_Authentication_Header.name: Authentication
